description:
An Introduction to Primer

Primer is the unified infrastructure for global payments. We give finance and payments teams the visibility and control to reduce complexity, improve performance, and capture more revenue - all from a single platform.

Backed by Sofina, Peak XV Partners, ICONIQ, Tencent, Accel, and Balderton, we're building the payments layer the world's best companies rely on.

Watch our showcase >

Read up on our $100m Series C

Learn more about our culture >

Which team will you be joining?

The merchant experience is only as good as the platform behind it — and most of that experience is the interface itself.

 

The Account Experience team builds and owns the full platform merchants use to interact with Primer — from initial setup through to day-to-day operations, and increasingly through Primer AI Companion as a first-class interface. The team spans several connected areas: Primer Companion, Merchant Account Setup, Monitors, Workflows, Auditing, and the cross-cutting concerns that keep the whole merchant experience cohesive.

 

As Staff Engineer you'll set front-end technical direction across these areas, not within a single one. You'll work across 2-3 teams, partner with multiple stakeholders, and stay hands-on in the implementation that matters most. The team runs a 'you build it, you own it' model: engineers own their work from design through to production.

 

The stack includes TypeScript, React, and modern front-end tooling, sitting on top of services in Python, AWS, Kubernetes, and Terraform.

 

What will you be doing?

  • Setting and driving front-end technical strategy across the Account Experience teams, from architecture and component-system decisions through to hands-on implementation where it counts

  • Owning the architecture of a complex, data-dense merchant platform — the patterns, state management, and performance characteristics that hold up as the surface area grows

  • Shaping how Primer AI Companion matures as a first-class merchant interface, including the front-end architecture that makes a conversational surface feel native to the platform

  • Holding the experience coherent across Account Setup, Monitors, Workflows, and Auditing — building the shared component and design-system foundations that stop the areas drifting apart

  • Leading engineers across teams without direct authority, through code, design reviews, and technical mentorship that raises the front-end bar around you

  • Owning the things that are easy to neglect: accessibility, performance budgets, and front-end observability as first-class concerns, not afterthoughts

  • Partnering with Product and Design, and with backend engineers across teams, to shape decisions where front-end constraints or opportunities are material

 

What We're Looking For

  • Demonstrable experience operating at staff or principal level: setting front-end technical direction across multiple teams, not just within one

  • Deep front-end engineering expertise with TypeScript and React, and a track record of architecting complex, long-lived web applications

  • Real fluency in the things that separate good front-end from great: state management at scale, performance, accessibility, and component-system design

  • The kind of judgment that earns trust fast — engineers follow your technical lead because you're right, not because of your title

  • Enough comfort across the stack to reason about the APIs and services your front-end depends on, and to partner with backend engineers as an equal

  • Strong written and verbal communication, including making complex technical decisions legible to Product, Design, and non-technical stakeholders

  • Comfort working in payments, fintech, or platform contexts is welcome, though depth of engineering matters more than the specific industry.

You May Not Like It Here If

  • You prefer a defined lane — at Staff level you'll be expected to find and shape the work across several teams, not wait for it to be handed to you

  • You think of front-end as the layer that just renders what the backend sends — here it's a first-class engineering discipline with real architectural weight

  • You want a QA team to catch your bugs — we don't have one, and we don't plan to

  • Remote-first feels like a compromise to you — for us it's deliberate, and it demands real discipline and strong async habits

 

✅ A typical interview process

  • An initial intro call with a Talent Partner

  • An interview with the Hiring Manager

  • Challenge Stage - Contextualised to the role

  • A final, values-alignment interview

What's the culture like at Primer?


We're building a culture where people can do their best work and be proud of the impact they have. You'll be working with people who are mission-driven, smart, and reflective, and who are genuinely invested in building exceptional products and delivering success for our merchants.

We work remotely, and have done since day one. We believe that building a successful, profitable company goes beyond proximity. We invest in our relationships through great remote working practices and thoughtfully designed face-to-face time, including workations, our annual company retreat, and access to co-working spaces across most major cities.

The work is challenging. Scaleups are a challenge, and building category-defining products is a challenge. But there's a meaningful difference between a challenge and a struggle. At Primer, the right challenge comes with the right support: strong onboarding, a collaborative environment, and a team that is genuinely invested in your success. It's never something you face alone.

title: Product Engineer (all levels)
description:
👋 Hi, I’m Sina, CTO at Nous. 

I’ve spent my entire career in startups, starting my first company when I was a teenager, and navigated many 0→1 journeys (including starting the largest social network of its time in my home country).

The common thread that led me here is finding complexity that wastes people’s time or money, then solving for making them disappear. And that’s exactly what Nous aims to do.

If this problem space resonates, please read on. 

PS: I’ve actually written this page with my hands; this is not AI-written content!

About Nous

Roughly 90% of UK households are overpaying on their bills. Nous is an agent to absorb complexity out of households, saving them money and time. Our mission is to make people’s lives simpler and fairer, starting with the 30 million households here in the UK, and soon far beyond.

Nous is growing fast, and it’s working. 20x YoY growth makes us one of the fastest scaling startups in the UK. And NPS of +70 (higher than Apple) shows that our users love it.

We’ve just launched two novel new products (on top of our current service lines). Insurance: we’re the first to get the regulatory approval and build the tech to actually do the full insurance discovery and purchase journey as an agent for the user (not just give them a link to the best deal). Subscription management: lots of companies use open banking to draw pretty graphs - we’re the first to use it to actively save people money starting by cancelling unwanted subscriptions for them.

It would be easy to look at this and think we’ve got it all figured out.

But we’ve only scratched the surface; our ambitions are SO much higher. We started with bills because ‘change begins at home’ - it’s a naturally low-interest, messy area of our lives which most of us don’t want to think about. Similar to how Amazon started with books as their first category to go after.

‘Talk is cheap. Action is what really matters’. What we’re building is an agent to take some of the load of life, make good decisions and act for us in areas we can’t or don’t want to act on our own. For an agent, advice is cheap. Action is the product. And action means solving problems in the messy real world.

A note on product

There’s ‘product’ as in the web application that guides our users through the complex world of bills and household admin. It acts as their interface to our management service, as well as all the behind the scenes capabilities needed to orchestrate and deliver that service - actually saving our users money and time. Try it here: app.nous.co/signup (it’s free!)

Then there’s ‘product’ as experienced by our users - which is a service which makes life simple and fair. To deliver this we’ve built a set of powerful capabilities that let us run and improve the service efficiently at scale: agentic communication, multimodal data extraction, orchestration for long-running operational processes, recommendations, our own agentic harness, and more. We compose these into executable workflows that deliver real outcomes for members, like switching someone to a better energy deal without the hassle.

Today, we help manage six areas of household spending: Energy, Mobile, Broadband, Mortgage, Personal finances (e.g., managing subscriptions), and Insurance. But we’re just getting started. Behind the scenes, we’ve built the technology (we call it Blueprints) that acts as rails for us to quickly expand on the breadth and depth of our service lines.

The role

We need your help building a world-class product that will be used regularly by millions of people; which means figuring out, together, what it really takes to absorb household complexity.

As a product engineer, we'll empower you with context to enable fast iterations, end-to-end ownership and lots of agency. You’ll be a hands-on technical leader on some of the highest-leverage areas of our codebase, from building out agentic capabilities to scaling our service logic.

Some examples of the types of problems you'll solve:

  • Anton led and shipped an entire product line around open banking and subscription management three months after joining. Yes, he had support from legal, design, commercial and his team (we even became FCA registered). But one product engineer still took it from idea to a best-in-class product in the category.

  • Ed led the our latest Blueprint architecture, which now powers every service line. Changes to complex, long-running workflows that once took weeks can now sometimes take minutes. All safely, reliably and with full type safety.

  • Tim led and shipped our car insurance product line, in less than 3 months. We built a journey where an agent performs the discovery and purchase journeys - something that's not been done before and needed problem solving at the intersection of engineering, product and regulatory.

  • As a team, we built our own agentic harness (we call it super-engineer); it’s enabled us to build faster, investigate complex cross-system issues effectively; and it self-improves.

There are also so many interesting problems we are in the infancy of solving. Just as an example - user’s trust us with their Open Banking data - but it’s just lists of transactions. How can we use that stream of information and combine it with all the other data we have, to reduce friction from their lives?

Every week, we’re building tools for ourselves and evolving how we work, to make ourselves more effective. I strongly believe in the value of compounding gains, and much of our focus goes into investing in what results in exponential growth.


Although our stack is constantly evolving (and you can help shape that), here’s a current snapshot:

  • Full-stack TypeScript, React, Postgres, and Temporal for long-running orchestration.

  • Infra: AWS, Terraform, strong observability via Sentry and Datadog (full-stack, not just logs).

  • Data: we lean heavily on Snowflake, Omni, dbt, Fivetran, Amplitude and Segment — and we’ve even built some of our own tooling to understand how well we’re helping our members.

  • And we use Github, Linear, Graphite, and Blacksmith every day. We choose the best tool for the job, and don’t obsess around specific technologies.

  • We also heavily rely on our wide range of agentic and tooling harness that we build and iterate on across the team. They’re part of the “secret” behind how we move fast, reliably.

You’ll report directly to the CTO (and we’ll work closely), so will be in the room for key architectural and product decisions. We’re deliberately light on layers of management: exceptional individual contributors shape direction by solving hard problems.


We organise around small product squads (around 5–7 people) with a single shared objective; and ship and learn fast.

You'll build in two modes

This is the bit that makes the role different, so it's worth being clear about.

Sometimes you build the product directly. That might mean a new product line, a core product improvement; or an exciting new idea to experiment on the product. You're usually working with one or two others, moving fast from a rough plan and jumping on problems as they surface.

Sometimes you build the multiplier. The safe surfaces and shared tooling that let a non-engineer ship without breaking things. Think the internal equivalent of what Lovable did for "anyone can put a website live", but for our problems: bills, switching, household admin at scale.

Both are hard engineering work. And the two feed each other: the better the multiplier you build, the more the genuinely deep problems are the ones left for you. Leverage for the ops team is leverage for you.

What we look for

You don't need to tick every box. If you read these and feel a mix of "this is me" and "this would stretch me", you're probably right for it.

  • You own problems end to end. You're happiest going from fuzzy pain to shipped fix to the numbers that show it worked. You instinctively ask "what's the smallest thing we can ship to learn?" instead of waiting for a perfect spec.

  • You think like a PM as much as an engineer. You care about the problem, the user, flow, UX, and even copy as much as correctness, because you've seen a small wording change flip confusion into action.

  • You're a pragmatic builder. Clean, practical code others can extend. You know when to abstract and when to keep it brutally simple to go fast. You'll happily delete your own code when reality disagrees with it.

  • You build leverage for other people. You explain complex things simply, you pair on gnarly problems, and you leave things clearer than you found them. You see a good tool that unblocks a teammate as real work, not a distraction from it.

  • You're here for the problem. Fairness, money and complexity, made manageable for people who don't have time to fight the system themselves. You'd rather work hard on something that genuinely helps.

We hire across all levels (mid-senior, to staff+), with a minimum 2 years of professional experience. The size and independence of your initial scope will reflect your experience, but the shape of the role is the same: you own outcomes. For earlier-career candidates, our assessment is primarily on your growth trajectory.

This probably isn't for you if…

  • You want a clear remit handed down before you can move. Here you get lots of context and invested colleagues, not a manager translating the work into tickets for you.

  • You believe nothing should ship unless it routes through a gate you personally control. The control we care about is structural: guardrails in the tools, not who's allowed to type. If that sounds too loose, we'll probably frustrate each other.

  • You want to specialise narrowly and stay in one layer. The role is broad by design.

What to expect

As CTO, and the person hiring for this role, you can hold me to these promises:

  • You’ll never be bored. You’ll continuously have difficult and interesting challenges to solve

  • The rest of the team and I will empower you with context, and will involve you as a co-founder

  • You’ll be learning every day, solve new challenges, and sometimes find yourself running while simultaneously learning how to run

  • You’ll have the space and support to grow your AI engineering skills, whether through harness engineering, trying new approaches, or even going as far as inventing new ways of solving problems. We’re building at the edge of what is possible, and we are conscious that there’s trial and error and first principles thinking involved in figuring it out

  • You’ll work closely with a caring and highly intelligent team. It’s ok, stalk us on Linkedin and check for yourself

Remuneration and benefits

Compelling packages, including meaningful share options with life-changing upside. We’ve raised enough money to pay real salaries. We're building something great together and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together.

An environment where you can do your best work:

  • 🏢 A great office set up for lots of collaborative working. We already need more whiteboards

  • 💻 The equipment / setup / training you need to do your best work (and of course, AI subscriptions, including Claude Code Max tier)

  • 🤝 A high-context environment with lots of exposure to the big decisions - be in the room when it happens (literally)

  • 🏡 Flexibility around remote work. If you sometimes just need to get your head down, that's fine

  • ☕ Very good coffee

  • 🍽️ A well-stocked kitchen (featuring a wildly popular toastie maker) so you can always make yourself a breakfast or light lunch on the house

  • 🎉 Informal social every week, something bigger every month, plus a set-piece event in the summer and again at Christmas - we're not robots!

  • ✈ 33 days paid holidays (including bank holidays)

  • 💊 Health and dental cash plans, including an employee assistance programme

  • 🚴 Travel benefits, (e.g., the cycle-to-work scheme)

  • 💰 A generous cash referral bonus if you introduce us to someone who joins the team

Nous has an office-first culture (i.e., at least 3 days a week, more context on it here). That means we encourage in-person working, and most people do work from the office in Farringdon most of the time. We do a lot of brainstorming, problem-solving and interaction within the team and presence makes this more effective. It also helps ensure people have good peripheral awareness and high context. But we are pragmatic not doctrinal about this, and recognise that some types of work can sometimes be done remotely.

title: Senior Backend Engineer
description:
About Us

Plentific is a property technology platform used by housing providers, local authorities, housing associations, asset managers, and contractors across the UK and Germany to coordinate repairs, maintenance, and contractor workflows at scale. The platform combines a marketplace, workflow automation, and operational analytics, and is built to handle the volume and compliance demands of social housing, local authority property portfolios, and large-scale residential operations.


We are headquartered in London and our team works across Europe.
We are growing the team to expand the platform's coverage across Europe and to integrate AI throughout the product and operating model. If you are interested in working on hard, real-world problems in a sector that has long been under-served by good software, we would like to hear from you.

The Role

This is a hands-on, fully remote role in one of Plentific's cross-functional product engineering teams. The Senior Backend Engineer works alongside product managers, frontend engineers, quality engineers, and other backend engineers to build and operate the services behind repairs, quoting and invoicing, payments, contractor search, messaging, notifications, and fraud prevention. The role is open across the European countries where we currently employ or engage remote engineers.


Our backend is built primarily in Python and Django, with Django REST Framework and FastAPI supporting APIs in a service-oriented architecture deployed on AWS and Kubernetes. PostgreSQL, Redis, and Celery underpin data-intensive and asynchronous workflows. The systems handle complex permissions, legacy integrations, high transaction volumes, and business processes where reliability and data correctness matter.


AI-assisted, spec-driven development is part of normal engineering practice at Plentific. The Senior Backend Engineer turns product requirements into implementation-ready specifications, uses agentic coding tools across implementation, testing, review, and documentation, and remains accountable for the resulting software. AI-generated output is held to the same standard as human-written code. Success means delivering reliable services, improving the codebase and engineering practice around the role, and enabling the wider team to ship confidently at pace.

Key Responsibilities

Backend Engineering

  • Build and maintain APIs, microservices, and data pipelines using Python, Django, Django REST Framework, FastAPI, and related platform tooling.

  • Design service boundaries, API contracts, relational data models, and integration flows for complex property operations. Produce ERDs and other technical diagrams where they make relationships, ownership, and system behaviour easier to review.

  • Develop asynchronous and event-driven workflows using technologies such as Celery and Redis.

  • Write complex SQL, evolve PostgreSQL schemas safely, and optimise database performance where customer experience or operational throughput depends on it.

  • Review, refactor, and retire existing code so it remains readable, testable, maintainable, and suitable for new product requirements.

Quality, Reliability, and Operations

  • Write automated tests at the appropriate level and integrate them into CI/CD so changes can be released with clear evidence of quality.

  • Instrument services with logs, metrics, traces, and alerts that make production behaviour and failures easy to understand.

  • Diagnose and resolve production incidents across services, databases, queues, integrations, and infrastructure.

  • Design for security, resilience, performance, and data integrity across business-critical workflows.

Agentic and Spec-Driven Development

  • Partner with product managers, frontend engineers, and quality engineers to turn agreed product behaviour into implementation-ready technical solution designs covering assumptions, alternatives, service interactions, data and schema changes, failure modes, security, observability, rollout, rollback, and tests.

  • Use agentic coding tools such as Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, or equivalent to generate, refactor, test, review, and document code within clear technical constraints.

  • Evaluate AI-generated code critically for correctness, maintainability, security, performance, and fit with Plentific's architecture.

  • Break specifications into small, reviewable changes and validate each change against its intended behaviour before release.

  • Improve the team's spec-driven development practice through reusable patterns, review checklists, examples, and concise documentation.

Delivery and Collaboration

  • Collaborate with product managers, frontend engineers, quality engineers, and other backend engineers from problem framing through release and production operation.

  • Surface technical risks and trade-offs early, and propose pragmatic changes to scope, design, or delivery plans.

  • Review code and technical designs, setting a high bar while giving feedback that helps other engineers improve.

  • Coach mid-level and junior engineers through pairing, code review, debugging, and design discussion.

Requirements

  • Expert-level Python and Django, with strong object-oriented design and software engineering fundamentals.

  • Strong command of API design, service-oriented architecture, distributed systems, and asynchronous processing.

  • Expert-level relational data modelling, including the ability to produce clear ERDs, define entities, relationships, constraints, and ownership, and design PostgreSQL schemas that balance correctness, performance, and safe evolution.

  • Demonstrable ability to turn incomplete product requirements into clear technical solution designs for complex backend changes, identifying assumptions and resolving ambiguity with product and engineering colleagues through concise written analysis and appropriate architecture, sequence, data-flow, and entity-relationship diagrams.

  • Sound judgement around automated testing, observability, production reliability, security, and data integrity.

  • Strong working fluency with agentic coding tools and spec-driven development workflows, including specification writing, code generation, test generation, and critical review.

  • Demonstrable ability to review technical designs and code, explain trade-offs, and coach less-experienced engineers.

  • Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts and delivery risks in plain English.

  • Pragmatic delivery judgement, balancing immediate product needs with the maintainability and scalability of a long-lived platform.

  • High ambition and a strong sense of urgency, with the drive to deliver an ambitious product roadmap at pace using AI, and a positive, can-do attitude.

Experience and Qualifications

  • 6+ years of professional software engineering experience, with substantial commercial experience in Python and Django.

  • Experience building and operating Django-based services in production on AWS and Kubernetes.

  • Experience with Django REST Framework or FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery, and CI/CD pipelines.

  • Track record of designing and safely evolving complex relational data models in a large, long-lived production codebase, using ERDs and written technical designs to align engineers and stakeholders while preserving design quality, testability, maintainability, and safe evolution.

  • Experience working in cross-functional product teams with shared ownership of customer outcomes and production operation.

  • Experience using AI coding tools in a professional software delivery workflow, ideally within a spec-driven development framework.

Benefits

We offer:

  • 25 days annual holiday, plus one additional day for every year served, up to a maximum of 5 additional days

  • Fully remote working, including the option to work abroad

  • Private healthcare for you and your immediate family, with discounted gym membership and access to optical, dental, and private GP services

  • Enhanced parental leave

  • Life insurance at 4× salary

  • Employee assistance programme

  • Company volunteering day and charity salary-sacrifice scheme

  • Learning management system powered by Udemy

  • Referral bonus and charity donation when someone you introduce joins the company

  • Season ticket loan, Cycle to Work, electric vehicle, and Techscheme programmes

  • Pension scheme

  • Company-sponsored dinners and social gatherings

title: Staff Product Manager, Agentic & AI Platform
description:
About us

Founded in 2019 and part of Y Combinator's 2020 cohort, Photoroom is the leading visual solution for e-commerce.

We've raised Series B funding and reached 300+ million users worldwide, processing over 5 billion images annually and serving both small businesses and major enterprises like Amazon, DoorDash, and Decathlon through our mobile app, web platform, and API.

We're a team of 100+ passionate builders giving e-commerce businesses superpowers to create visuals that help them grow, making the hardest parts of selling online disappear. We focus on craft, innovation, and collaboration to create exceptional impact for e-commerce businesses worldwide.

Role Summary

We're looking for a Staff Product Manager to own the AI platform every Photoroom product is built on. Our mission is that any team ships best-in-class GenAI visuals without needing a backend engineer: the primitives, the gateway and the no-code tooling turn adding an AI capability into a configuration step rather than an engineering project. On top of that sits the agentic layer — multi-step visual workflows that generate, check, reason, route and publish on their own. Working closely with engineers, ML researchers, and the product teams who ship on your platform, you'll decide what gets built, why, and how it ships.

Location: Paris, (Hybrid)

About the role

  • Own the platform every AI feature runs through. Expand and improve our AI gateway, including safeguards, evals, cost and observability, giving teams the ability to ship with little to no code and build skills that we can ship directly to users.

  • Build the agentic layer and Photoroom’s MCP. Visual agents that run multi-step flows: generate, QA, route, retry, publish, all unattended and at catalog scale.

  • Define the problem before the solution. Sharpen the problem, then partner with engineering and research to ship work that feels effortless — for the developers and PMs using the platform as much as for end users.

  • Treat other teams as your customers. Every team's roadmap contains AI features gated on platform work. You'll prioritise across them, hold a strategy rather than a request queue, and say no with reasons.

  • Turn AI capabilities into products people want. Work hand-in-hand with our researchers and engineers to convert new model capabilities into shipped features that move usage and revenue, and turn them into primitives other teams can reuse.

  • Use data to decide, not to justify. Pull and interpret data yourself, such as adoption, latency, inference cost per successful generation, eval results. Form hypotheses, measure what shipped, and call what's next. You won't need to wait around for someone else to run the query.

About You

  • You've shipped products users love. 10+ years as a PM, with multiple launches where you have solved a user’s problem and delivered business outcomes.

  • You've built platform, infrastructure or developer-facing products. APIs, SDKs, internal platforms, ML infrastructure — products whose users are engineers.

  • You've shipped something agentic or model-backed into production. You understand evals, guardrails, non-deterministic output, cost per call, and what breaks when a multi-step flow runs unattended a million times.

  • AI has reshaped how you work. You use Claude or equivalent every day, for prototyping, testing with users, or automating the parts of the job that used to fill your calendar. The value you bring sits in strategy and direction, not in writing tickets.

  • You have demonstrable product taste. You can show specific work where the details matter and explain the calls you made, including the ones you'd make differently now. On a platform, taste shows up in the interface you make other people build against.

  • You create clarity from ambiguity. Given a fuzzy problem, you take action rather than waiting for direction: you structure it, decide what matters, and move.

  • You're data-fluent. You pull, interpret, and challenge data yourself, and use it to form a point of view rather than confirm one.

  • You thrive in small teams with high autonomy. You can ship without being managed, and can operate in a remote, async-first environment that offers no scaffolding around you.

Benefits

  • 25 days + 8–10 RTT

  • Competitive equity package with stock options/BSPCE, giving you ownership in our growing company

  • €1000 one-time home office grant OR €400 per month co-working space stipend

  • €1,000 annual learning and development budget for training, courses, books, and skill development

  • Private health insurance

  • Access to personalised mental health support, including 1:1 sessions with therapists or coaches, self-care tools, and well-being resources via MokaCare

  • Sports and cultural activities reimbursement

  • Relocation support (up to 10k) available for those choosing to move to France, including apartment finding and visa assistance

Note: Visa sponsorship and relocation support are only available for positions based in France.

Hiring Process

  1. Screening call with Talent Manager (30min)

  2. Technical interview with Hiring Manager (60min)

  3. Take-home assignment (duration varies by role) and live review with the team (90min)

  4. Culture fit interviews and meet the team (~3h in total)

  5. Reference check and offer

Support: We value diversity and aim to create an inclusive experience for all applicants. Please let us know if there's anything we can do to make the process more accessible for you.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging

We're committed to enabling everyone to feel included and valued at work. We believe our company and culture are strongest when composed of diverse experiences and backgrounds.

That's also why we have flexible working hours, trust people to work in a hybrid environment, and extended parental leave.

All qualified applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, family, gender identity, marital status, national origin, physical or mental disability, sex (including pregnancy), sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws.

Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains.

Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times.

To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies.

BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America.

Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard.

About the role

Delta builds BLP’s core software: the technical foundation that everything else at the company runs on.

Who we're looking for

Modelling logic and correctness by construction is paramount to us. We aim to express what must be true, prevent invalid states, and keep systems pristine even as they grow.

Thus, we’re looking for highly ambitious engineers who can tackle difficult problems and think precisely. You must be able to make assumptions explicit and use formal, structured reasoning to reach a solution, and explain why it is correct. Typically, strong background in mathematics is a key foundation for this kind of work. We also place a high value on thoroughness and perfectionism.

Tooling wise, we rely heavily on type systems & functional programming.

 

What you'll do

Our work spans four areas, you will usually work on a given project within one of:

  • Infrastructure: Build and operate the cloud infrastructure BLP depends on, covering security, observability and CI/CD.

  • Backend: Develop a large codebase, tackling performance, concurrency and the challenges of distributed systems.

  • ML: Apply the latest AI technology to complex, real-world business problems and turn it into reliable production software.

  • Unbound: Build our product extension platform, enabling BLP to automate arbitrary customer business processes as we scale.

 

What you'll bring

We do not require experience with any particular technology or even industry software development experience.

You should, however, provide clear evidence of the abilities we’re looking for. That evidence could include:

  • strong academic backgrounds (math PhD/MSc or significant olympiad achievements)

  • startup experience (early employee, built productive systems yourself & know what it takes to maintain them)

  • FP experience (have deep understanding of programming languages and are able to discern the various tradeoffs of different paradigms)

 

What we value

We value engineers who think deeply about systems, care about correctness, and take pride in building infrastructure that is understandable, maintainable, and reliable.

Flexibility. Work on-site in Zurich or remotely within Europe.

 
 

Learn more about blp and our values at blp.digital/company/careers.

title: Senior Backend Engineer, Shopping Agents
description:
Senior Backend Engineer, Shopping Agents

Sage AI Labs · Munich · Full-time · [Remote]

About us

Sage AI Labs is building the infrastructure that lets AI agents transact on the open web. It is one of the few genuinely unsolved problems left in commerce, and whoever solves it sets the defaults everyone else builds on top of.

The company was founded by Sebastian Thrun (founder of Google X and Waymo, Udacity) and is backed by leading venture and strategic investors.

About the role

We build agents that shop for you. They find products across the open web and complete the purchase end to end. Real carts, real payments, and real systems built to stop them.

You would own that. Architecture, code, deploys, monitoring, and on-call for systems that transact around the clock, working directly with our CTO.

What you'll own

Our checkout agents. Frontier-model computer-use agents driving live checkouts at scale, plus the machinery that keeps them standing when the ground moves. Every retailer breaks differently and they change without warning. Your job is to make failure rare and recovery automatic.

Ingestion at scale. Take product ingestion from hundreds of sources to thousands. The answer is not more hand-written code. It is infrastructure that generates, validates, and monitors itself.

Search and ranking. Embedding-based retrieval, LLM query understanding, reranking, and caching, across a catalog that never stops changing.

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years building backend and infrastructure systems, with strong Python

  • You have owned production systems end to end: deploys, databases, observability, and the pager. You have been the person who got paged, and you fixed the class of problem rather than the incident

  • You like adversarial problems. Systems where something on the other side is actively working against you

  • You take correctness seriously because the stakes are real. These systems spend customers' money, so a silent failure is a wrong order, not a red build

  • You can move without a finished spec. We are small, and the roadmap changes when the market does

Nice to have

  • Built AI-first products or LLM-based agents in production, not just in a prototype

  • Working knowledge of classic ML and deep learning, enough to reason about retrieval and ranking rather than only calling an API

  • Background in e-commerce, payments, or fraud and risk infrastructure

Why this role

Very few engineers get to own a category-defining system while the category is still being defined. This is one of those seats, at the point where it still counts as early. A year from now this problem will have a standard answer and someone will have written it. We intend for that to be us.
